zeit.description: Julian Nagelsmann hat seinen WM-Kader vorgestellt. Mit Manuel Neuer im Tor, einem finnischen Muttersprachler und einem Stürmer, der Esel liebt. Das sind die 27 WM-Fahrer.

zeit.description: Auf Facebook waren einem Mann fälschlicherweise Kriegsverbrechen unterstellt worden. Meta löschte den Post nur verzögert und muss dafür 100.000 Euro Ordnungsgeld zahlen.

france24fr.title: C’est la dernière Coupe du monde de ces légendes
france24fr.description:
⏳ Une page du foot est sur le point de se tourner. 
 
Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Didier Deschamps... Le #Mondial2026 sera leur dernière Coupe du monde. 
 
🌟 Retour sur l’héritage laissé par ces géants du football et sur ce qu’ils représentent pour l’histoire de la compétition. 
 
🎙️ Analyse avec Benoît Perrochais.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : l'Iran annonce une "cessation" des frappes contre Israël
Israël : le pays à l'arrêt après des tirs de missiles iraniens
france24fr.description: Israël s’est réveillé sous les sirènes d’alerte après des tirs de missiles iraniens visant plusieurs grandes villes, dont Jérusalem. L’État hébreu a riposté, tandis que les écoles ont été fermées et plusieurs vols suspendus dans un climat de très forte tension régionale, alors que Donald Trump appelle à éviter une nouvelle escalade et que le gouvernement israélien reste silencieux pour le moment. Les précisions de la correspondante de France 24 Noga Tarnopolsky.

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : symbole des failles de la justice française
france24fr.description: La mort de Lyhanna, 11 ans, retrouvée après sa disparition dans le Gers, a provoqué une forte émotion et ravivé les critiques sur la protection de l’enfance en France. Le principal suspect aurait déjà fait l’objet de plusieurs plaintes pour viols, dont le traitement par la justice est aujourd’hui mis en cause dans le cadre de l’enquête. Ce drame relance plus largement le débat sur les défaillances du système judiciaire face aux violences sexuelles sur mineurs.

france24fr.title: Un drone s'écrase en Moldavie, un autre abattu par l'Otan en Lettonie
france24fr.description: Un drone s'est écrasé lundi dans un champ de l'est de la Moldavie, quelques jours seulement après l'explosion d'un drone maritime dans le port de Constanta en Roumanie voisine. En Lettonie, deux chasseurs français ont abattu un drone qui avait pénétré l'espace aérien letton.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : un nouvel embrasement régional qui fragilise l'avenir politique de Trump
france24fr.description: À l’approche des midterms, la reprise des hostilités au Moyen-Orient complique la position de Donald Trump, qui semble perdre la maîtrise de l’escalade et appelle à un arrêt des combats, conscient des risques politiques pour son avenir. Les explications d'Antoine Mariotti, chroniqueur international chez France 24, qui revient aussi sur la relation de Trump avec le Premier ministre israélien Benjamin Netanyahu.

france24fr.title: Philippines : un puissant séisme de magnitude 7,8 fait au moins 15 morts
france24fr.description: Un puissant séisme de magnitude 7,8 dans le sud des Philippines a fait au moins quinze morts, selon les autorités, et provoqué l'effondrement de nombreux bâtiments lundi matin, jour de la rentrée scolaire dans cet archipel d'Asie du sud-est.

france24fr.title: Je t'aime, moi non plus : Trump va assister au match 3 des finales NBA, une présence historique
france24fr.description: Supporter de longue date des New York Knicks, Donald Trump a confirmé qu'il assisterait lundi soir au premier match des finales NBA à New York depuis 1999 – une présence qui va entraîner un renforcement considérable des mesures de sécurité. Le président a une relation contrastée avec la NBA, dont les récents champions ont décliné les invitations pour la traditionnelle réception à la Maison Blanche.

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : un fiasco judiciaire
france24fr.description: Après l’affaire Lyhanna et les révélations sur des plaintes pour violences sexuelles visant le principal suspect, Gérald Darmanin réunit les procureurs généraux pour exiger une révision de l’ensemble des plaintes concernant des enfants victimes, soit environ 70.000 dossiers. france24fr.title: Nouvelle flambée de tensions entre l’Iran et Israël
france24fr.description: Israël a mené dans la nuit des frappes contre plusieurs cibles militaires et énergétiques en Iran, après des tirs de missiles iraniens visant notamment Tel-Aviv et Jérusalem. Téhéran affirme avoir riposté aux récents bombardements israéliens sur la banlieue sud de Beyrouth et menace désormais d’intensifier ses attaques contre l’État hébreu.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : arrivée chaotique de l'Irak aux États-Unis, la politique de visas en question
france24fr.description: Visas restreints pour assister à la Coupe du monde aux États-Unis, nouveaux épisodes. Lors de l'arrivée de la sélection irakienne sur le sol américain, son attaquant star, Aymen Hussein, a été retenu plusieurs heures à la douane. Quant à son photographe officiel, il a été interdit d'entrée dans le pays de Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Le Pape Léon au Parlement espagnol pour un discours historique
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon est en visite en Espagne. Il doit se rendre au Parlement pour prononcer un discours consacré à la paix et à la polarisation politique, avant de rencontrer des victimes de violences sexuelles au sein de l’Église. Les précisions de Maude Petit-Jové, à Madrid.

france24fr.title: Xi Jinping en Corée du Nord : démonstration de force diplomatique en Asie
france24fr.description: La visite de Xi Jinping en Corée du Nord est perçue comme un baromètre des relations de la Chine en Asie et de sa stratégie régionale face aux États-Unis. Pékin et Pyongyang entretiennent une relation particulière, fondée sur un traité d’amitié et d’assistance mutuelle, tandis que la Chine reste le principal soutien économique et politique du régime nord-coréen. france24fr.title: Liban : Nabatiyé, nouvelle cible de l'armée israélienne ?
france24fr.description: Ce week-end, l’armée israélienne a multiplié les frappes dans le sud du Liban, notamment autour de Tyr et de Nabatiyé, ville considérée comme l’un des principaux bastions du Hezbollah dans le sud du pays et qui semble désormais devenir une cible centrale de l’offensive israélienne, comme l'explique Serge Berberi. Ces bombardements interviennent dans un contexte de forte escalade régionale, marqué par de nouveaux échanges de tirs et de missiles entre l’Iran et Israël

france24fr.title: Vollering renverse le Giro, les Messines au sommet, Wemby dans le dur : les infos sport du week-end
france24fr.description: ⁠Metz a ​remporté la première ​Ligue des championnes de l'histoire du handball français grâce ​à ‌sa victoire ⁠en finale contre le ‌club hongrois de Györ (31-29), double tenant ⁠du titre. Les Spurs de Victor Wembanyama ont encore été défaits vendredi à domicile par les Knicks (105-104) et se retrouvent en position très délicate dans la finale NBA. france24fr.title: 100 jours de guerre au Moyen-Orient : une facture économique de plus en plus lourde
france24fr.description: Cent jours après le début de la guerre au Moyen-Orient et la quasi-fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz, les marchés ont évité le scénario catastrophe sur le pétrole. Mais derrière cette relative résistance, les économies de la région ralentissent fortement et certaines plongent déjà dans la récession.

france24fr.title: Aires protégées, lutte contre les plastiques : la France annonce de nouvelles mesures pour l'océan
france24fr.description: Le gouvernement français a annoncé lundi la création de nouvelles aires de protection marine, et lancera un plan de lutte contre les déchets plastiques, dans le cadre d'un sommet à Paris un an après la Conférence des Nations unies sur l'océan, à Nice.

nzz.title: Israel schlägt nach Irans Raketenangriff zurück: Die Waffenruhe im Nahen Osten ist vorbei
nzz.description: Israel greift militärische Ziele an, während Iran am Montagmorgen weitere Raketen auf Israel abgefeuert hat. Donald Trump fordert ein sofortiges Ende der Kämpfe – und bringt den Einsatz von Bodentruppen ins Spiel.

nzz.description: Seit April gilt eine Waffenruhe zwischen Israel und Iran – doch nun greifen sich die beiden Staaten wieder gegenseitig an. Die Folgen des Konflikts sind weltweit spürbar. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Live-Ticker.

nzz.description: Einst als Droge der Schönen und Reichen bekannt, ist Kokain längst in allen Bevölkerungsschichten angekommen. Laut der jüngsten Analyse der Stiftung Sucht Schweiz nimmt der Konsum hierzulande weiter zu. Wer ist am meisten betroffen?

nzz.description: Staatsanwälte halten die Siegelung von digitalen Geräten für den Hauptgrund, dass Strafverfahren so lange dauern. Im Fall des Winterthurer Anschlags sei dies sogar eine Gefahr für die Sicherheit.

nzz.description: Jetlag, Klima, frühe Anspielzeiten: Die Fussball-WM in den USA, Kanada und Mexiko stellt die Schweizer Delegation vor viele Herausforderungen.

nzz.description: Ein starkes Erdbeben hat die südlichen Philippinen erschüttert und kleinere Tsunami-Wellen ausgelöst. Das Ausmass der Schäden und die Zahl der Todesopfer sind noch unklar.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ein französischer Kampfjet schiesst in Lettland ein unbemanntes Fluggerät ab – die wichtigsten Antworten zu den abgestürzten Drohnen im Norden Europas
nzz.description: Russlands Krieg gegen die Ukraine macht sich in Nordeuropa verstärkt bemerkbar. In den letzten Wochen kamen mehrmals ukrainische Drohnen vom Kurs ab.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Der Ski-Weltverband braucht eine neue Führung – Johan Eliasch ist der falsche Mann für den Job
nzz.description: Die Kündigung des Schweizers Urs Lehmann als FIS-CEO ist die finale Bestätigung: Der Ski-Weltverband braucht einen umfassenden personellen Neustart.

nzz.title: Wahlen in Armenien: Prorussische Parteien erleiden eine Niederlage
nzz.description: Trotz dem Fiasko in den Karabach-Kriegen erringt Ministerpräsident Nikol Paschinjan den dritten Wahlsieg in Folge und kann weiterregieren. Armenien bleibt damit auf Westkurs.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - So teuer ist Ihr Einkauf bei Aldi, Rewe und Co. geworden
nzz.description: Sie haben das Gefühl, alles wird teurer? Vergleichen Sie Ihren Kassenzettel von heute mit dem gleichen Einkauf von 2022 in deutschen Supermärkten – und erleben Sie Ihren persönlichen Preisschock.

nzz.title: Parlamentswahl in Kosovo: Albin Kurtis linksnationale Partei siegt mit deutlichem Verlust
nzz.description: Nach der dritten Parlamentswahl innerhalb von fünfzehn Monaten droht Kosovo in die nächste politische Blockade zu rutschen. Das ist frustrierend für die Bevölkerung und könnte teuer werden.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Wie beliebt ist Donald Trump?
nzz.description: Täglich aktualisierte Umfragewerte zeigen, wie die Amerikaner derzeit zur Amtsführung ihres Präsidenten stehen. Eine Übersicht in Grafiken.

nzz.title: Iran-Krieg: Bilder zeigen die Zerstörung nach Angriffen – und wie das Leben trotzdem weitergeht
nzz.description: Mit koordinierten Luftangriffen gegen Ziele in Iran haben Israel und die USA eine neue Phase der Eskalation im Nahen Osten eingeläutet. Die Gewalt bestimmt das Leben der Einwohner, von Teheran über Jerusalem bis nach Beirut. Die neuesten Entwicklungen in Bildern.

spiegel.title: Sean Penn: Warum der Hollywood-Star die Oscars bewusst fernblieb
spiegel.description: Smalltalk, Selfies und Preisverleihungen lösen bei Sean Penn Unbehagen aus. Kein Wunder also, dass er zuletzt die Oscar-Gala geschwänzt hat und stattdessen in Kyjiw war. Aus der Ferne habe er die Veranstaltung erstmals genossen.

spiegel.title: USA: Siegeszug der Populisten bei den Demokraten - Wie Donald Trump, nur sehr weit links
spiegel.description: Wie schlägt man den Feind im Weißen Haus? Indem man seinen Populismus kopiert, sagen linke US-Demokraten. Sie sind damit erstaunlich erfolgreich.

spiegel.description: Der SPD-Spitzenkandidat Jochen Ott möchte das Hamburger Schulsystem in NRW einführen und Markus Söder die späten Sommerferien abjagen. Reicht das, um im Wahlkampf gegen Hendrik Wüst zu bestehen?

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Deshalb kann Iran immer noch mit Raketen angreifen
spiegel.description: Trump behauptet, Irans Raketenprogramm zerstört zu haben. Nun aber greift das Regime erneut Israel an. Sicherheitsexperte Timur Kadyshev erklärt, was Teheran kann – und wo die Schwachstellen der US-Verteidigung liegen.

spiegel.description: Nach zwei Jahren Verzögerung stellt Apple eine neue KI-Version von Siri vor, der Erfolgsdruck ist hoch. Warum der Konzern ein Wagnis eingeht und was von dem neuen Modell zu erwarten ist.

spiegel.description: In Teheran wehrt sich der preisgekrönte Regisseur Jafar Panahi gegen eine Verurteilung wegen angeblicher »Propaganda gegen das System«. Ein berüchtigter Richter zeigt sich unerbittlich.

spiegel.title: Landgericht Frankfurt verhängt Ordnungsgeld gegen Meta
spiegel.description: Meta muss wegen zu später Löschung falscher Behauptungen auf Facebook ein Ordnungsgeld von 100.000 Euro zahlen. Das Gericht wertete die Erklärungsversuche des Konzerns sogar straferhöhend.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM: Uno-Klimasekretariat warnt vor extremer Hitze
spiegel.description: Hohe Temperaturen werden ein prägendes Element der Fußball-WM, da ist sich das Uno-Klimasekretariat sicher. Die größte Gefahr könne außerhalb der Stadien lauern.

spiegel.description: Beim Formel-1-Rennen in Monaco wurden gegen ungewöhnlich viele Piloten Zeitstrafen wegen zu hohen Tempos in der Boxengasse verhängt. Das will ein Team nachträglich anfechten.

spiegel.title: Euro-Einführung: Ging der deutsche Beitritt auf Kosten der Verbündeten?
spiegel.description: Ein internes AA-Papier zeigt: Deutschland erzielte in der Nato die höchste Friedensdividende nach 1990 – und verschaffte sich damit einen Vorteil bei der Euroeinführung.

spiegel.title: Armenien: Regierung von Nikol Paschinjan nach Parlamentswahl gestärkt
spiegel.description: Armeniens Regierungschef Paschinjan probt seit Längerem die Abkehr von Russland und eine Annäherung an die EU. Bei den Parlamentswahlen holte seine Partei den Sieg. Aus dem Kreml folgt prompt eine giftige Warnung.

spiegel.description: Die Stahlindustrie an der Saar steht vor einem Milliardenumbau. Doch die wechselnden Aussagen der Bundesregierung zur Umweltpolitik sind nach Ansicht von Ministerpräsidentin Anke Rehlinger Gift für den Fortschritt.

spiegel.title: Nasa: Diese Prada-Unterwäsche sollen Astronauten auf der Mondmission tragen
spiegel.description: Die Luxusmarke Prada hat für die US-Raumfahrtbehörde Unterwäsche mit Schläuchen entwickelt. Sie soll bei der Mondmission drei wichtige Aufgaben erfüllen – PR und Imagepflege nicht eingerechnet.

spiegel.title: Shakira: Sängerin wehrt sich gegen gefälschte Wahlkampfbilder in Kolumbien
spiegel.description: Im kolumbianischen Wahlkampf waren Bilder aufgetaucht, die den Kandidaten Iván Cepeda mit Shakira zeigen. Die Sängerin nennt die Kampagne einen Fake und wünscht dem Land eine friedliche Wahl.

observador.description: O número de partos voltou a subir em 2025: nasceram mais 87.130 crianças em Portugal, sendo o Norte a região que mais contribuiu, seguida de Lisboa. A proporção de mães estrangeiras aumentou 2,5%.

observador.description: Trata-se do sétimo desembolso ao abrigo do mecanismo para apoiar a recuperação e progresso da Ucrânia na adesão à UE, que soma já 29,5 mil milhões de euros — 77% da verba disponível para apoio.

observador.description: Comitiva iraniana aterrou este domingo no México, onde vai ficar durante o Mundial, sendo que ainda não sabe se pode entrar nos EUA na véspera dos jogos. Todos usaram um pin que lembra um ataque.

observador.title: Uma pessoa detida por tráfico de droga em Pombal
observador.description: 45 elementos policiais efetuam esta segunda-feira uma operação de combate ao tráfico de droga em Pombal da qual já resultou um detido. Investigação mantém-se em curso, diz PSP de Leiria.

new-sci.description: From dementia to heart attacks, hearing loss has been linked to a wide range of effects across the body, and the condition is on the rise. Fortunately, we're learning how best to safeguard this crucial sense and how we might be able to reverse the damage

new-sci.title: The looming El Niño could be bad – but much worse is to come
new-sci.description: Global warming will amplify the impacts of El Niño events, and could also make them much stronger and more far-reaching

new-sci.title: Stonehenge's altar stone probably wasn't transported by a glacier

phys-org.title: Nickelate superconductors share a common electronic fingerprint
phys-org.description: Superconductors, materials that conduct electricity with zero electrical resistance at specific temperature ranges, have proved very promising for the development of quantum computers and other cutting-edge technologies. While most of these materials become superconducting at very low temperatures, others exhibit superconductivity at higher temperatures.

phys-org.title: A 7.8 magnitude quake in the Philippines kills at least 19, fells buildings and sets off a tsunami
phys-org.description: An offshore magnitude 7.8 earthquake rocked the southern Philippines Monday, killing at least 19 people, injuring more than 200 others mostly in damaged buildings and sending a 1-meter (3-foot) tsunami into nearby coasts.

phys-org.title: Superheated magma may explain why similar volcanoes erupt in very different ways
phys-org.description: Scientists have shed light on a thermal process in magma that may help explain why similar volcanic systems can produce very different eruptive behaviors.

phys-org.title: Ancient dental calculus uncovers regional and historical shifts in Japan's oral microbiome
phys-org.description: Researchers have characterized the oral microbiomes of the Japanese population across time by analyzing the DNA preserved in dental calculus of human skeletal remains. The researchers compared microbial composition in dental calculus primarily from Edo-period individuals with that of modern dental calculus, and identified differences associated with time period, region, and the phylogeny of several oral bacterial species. The findings show that dental calculus can provide new avenues for examini

phys-org.title: Antibiotics drive resistance in waterways—even after they break down
phys-org.description: Antibiotics continue to drive resistance in bacteria, even after they are broken down in wastewater treatment plants and discharged into rivers and seas, new research published on World Oceans Day has shown for the first time.

phys-org.title: Solar panels on rewetted peatland could be a climate and nature win–win
phys-org.description: Researchers in Germany have found that solar panels on rewetted peatland provide a unique habitat for bird species along with generating green energy and potentially locking up carbon. Installing solar panels on rewetted peatlands is a new type of land use, providing a way to generate green energy and reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Now, research from the University of Greifswald has found that this novel land use may also benefit nature. The findings are published in Ecological Solutions and E

phys-org.title: Mysterious signals keep coming from space: Astronomers find their 'Rosetta stone'
phys-org.description: A pair of stars spiraling around each other. That's the origin of a new source of repeating radio bursts we've detected, called ASKAP J1745.

phys-org.title: AI spots smuggled seahorses, shark fins and sea cucumbers with 92% accuracy
phys-org.description: When we think of wildlife trafficking, we might think of rhino horns or baby orangutans sold as pets—but the smuggling of sea creatures, a less well-known crime, is just as damaging to marine ecosystems. Unfortunately, many commonly smuggled marine wildlife items, like shark fins, can be hidden in baggage or parcels and carried across borders with relative ease, without being detected. To get around this, scientists used AI to develop an algorithm that can detect samples of commonly trafficked s

phys-org.title: 'All-in-one' platform developed for multiple trait stacking in crops
phys-org.description: A major goal of modern crop breeding is to efficiently combine multiple desirable traits by "stacking" the favorable gene variants (alleles) that contribute to those traits in a single crop variety. However, current strategies are often time-consuming and inefficient.

phys-org.title: Could the Milky Way's missing mass be hiding in a swarm of interstellar comets?
phys-org.description: 3I/ATLAS has caused quite a stir over the last year, inviting astronomers to update what they know about other solar systems as well as our own. However, this third interstellar visitor may have an unexpected impact on our understanding of dark matter. A new paper, available on the arXiv preprint server from researchers at the University of Hamburg, attempts to calculate the impact that the presence of large amounts of interstellar objects, or ISOs, would have on our calculation of dark matter i

phys-org.title: How gene swapping helped build the planet's decomposers
phys-org.description: Decomposers are crucial for keeping Earth habitable, breaking down dead biomass and returning key nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus, to the ecosystem. Most decomposers, including fungi, survive through osmotrophy—a means of feeding by absorbing dissolved nutrients rather than engulfing prey. But how this method of feeding repeatedly arose across the eukaryotic tree of life remains unclear.

phys-org.title: In Brazil's Cerrado region, Indigenous fire practices reshape wildfire strategy
phys-org.description: Fire began crackling like approaching rain on a recent morning in the Xerente Indigenous Territory in Tocantins in northern Brazil. But the Indigenous residents weren't afraid and didn't rush to put it out.

phys-org.title: Lunar orbiter concept could reveal five key elements across moon in two years
phys-org.description: Researchers from Tokyo Metropolitan University have used simulations to show that a newly developed, compact X-ray telescope could be used to map the chemical composition of the entire lunar surface, a vital breakthrough for understanding its geological evolution. Detailed modeling of the detector and a realistic satellite mission show that two years would be enough to map five key elements, while an array of 5-by-5 detectors could improve resolution and get results faster.

phys-org.title: Continuous stirring made early life-like RNA systems more extinction-prone, experiment shows
phys-org.description: Recent research showed that an artificially constructed self-replicating RNA system modeling primitive life at the origin of life evolved to become more prone to extinction under certain experimental conditions.

phys-org.title: Dynamic terahertz wavefront control using stretchable single-walled carbon nanotube-based metasurfaces
phys-org.description: The terahertz (THz) frequency regime, sitting between microwaves and infrared light, has long promised revolutionary advances in wireless communication, security imaging and nondestructive sensing. A key roadblock, however, has been the lack of compact, dynamically tunable components capable of manipulating THz beams on demand.

phys-org.title: 'Flawless on the outside, flipped within': Detecting hidden defects in 2D dielectrics with light
phys-org.description: A material may appear flawless on the surface yet fail to function properly. The cause lies in structural defects hidden within two-dimensional thin films, which are considered key materials for next-generation semiconductor devices. Recently, a Korean research team developed an optical analysis method that can identify these invisible defects using light.

phys-org.title: Wonderwerk Cave bones reveal possible fire use by human ancestors 1.79 million years ago
phys-org.description: The discovery of fire was a major milestone in human evolution, giving our ancestors a way to stay warm, ward off predators, and eventually start cooking food. But exactly when this first happened is still intensely debated, as unambiguous evidence is difficult to find.

phys-org.title: A faster way to forecast alien weather
phys-org.description: The TRAPPIST-1 system, located about 41 light years from Earth, has been a focal point of much exoplanetary discussion—mainly because it has seven confirmed planets orbiting a dim M-dwarf star. Two of those planets—TRAPPIST-1e and -1f—are thought to be in the star's habitable zone. However, the habitable zone of M-dwarfs is so close to the star itself, the planets are likely tidally locked to it, meaning they have a permanent day and night side, with a "twilight terminator" in between.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.
